title: Biology — Variation and evolution

final_note: You worked through Biology — Variation and evolution — 23 specification statements.

concepts.def: The characteristics of an organism. The phenotype develops as a result of the genome of the organism and its interaction with the environment.

Differences in the characteristics of individuals in a population. Variation may be due to the genes they have inherited (genetic causes), the conditions in which they have developed (environmental causes), or a combination of genes and the environment.

A change in the DNA of an organism. All variants arise from mutations, and mutations occur continuously. Very rarely a mutation will lead to a new phenotype, and if that new phenotype is suited to an environmental change it can lead to a relatively rapid change in the species.

concepts.term: Effect of mutations on the phenotype
concepts.def: There is usually extensive genetic variation within a population of a species. Of the variants that arise from mutations, most have no effect on the phenotype, some influence phenotype and very few determine phenotype.
A change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time through a process of natural selection, which may result in the formation of a new species.

The process by which variants that give rise to phenotypes best suited to their environment are the most likely to survive and to breed successfully, so that the genes for these characteristics are passed on to the next generation.

concepts.term: Theory of evolution by natural selection
concepts.def: The theory that all species of living things have evolved from simple life forms that first developed more than three billion years ago.
Two populations of one species have formed two new species when they become so different in phenotype that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

The process by which humans breed plants and animals for particular genetic characteristics. Parents with the desired characteristic are chosen from a mixed population and bred together; from the offspring, those with the desired characteristic are bred together, and this continues over many generations until all the offspring show the desired characteristic. Humans have done this for thousands of years, since they first bred food crops from wild plants and domesticated animals.

The characteristic that humans select for in selective breeding, chosen for usefulness or appearance. Examples are disease resistance in food crops, animals which produce more meat or milk, domestic dogs with a gentle nature, and large or unusual flowers.
Breeding from closely related individuals, which selective breeding can lead to. Some breeds produced in this way are particularly prone to disease or inherited defects.

A process which involves modifying the genome of an organism by introducing a gene from another organism to give a desired characteristic. Genes from the chromosomes of humans and other organisms can be 'cut out' and transferred to cells of other organisms.

Crops that have had their genes modified by genetic engineering. GM crops include ones that are resistant to insect attack or to herbicides, and GM crops generally show increased yields. Plant crops have also been genetically engineered to be resistant to diseases or to produce bigger better fruits. Concerns about GM crops include the effect on populations of wild flowers and insects, and some people feel that the effects of eating GM crops on human health have not been fully explored.
Bacterial cells that have been genetically engineered to produce useful substances, such as human insulin to treat diabetes.
Modern medical research is exploring the possibility of genetic modification to overcome some inherited disorders.

In genetic engineering, the structure that carries the required gene into cells, usually a bacterial plasmid or a virus. Enzymes are used to isolate the required gene, the gene is inserted into the vector, and the vector is used to insert the gene into the required cells. Genes are transferred to the cells of animals, plants or microorganisms at an early stage in their development so that they develop with the desired characteristics.

mcqs.q: Two plants grown from cuttings of the same parent plant are given different amounts of light. One grows much taller than the other. What does this difference show?
options: The plants inherited different genes for their height
The change in light has caused a mutation in one plant
The environment has influenced the phenotype of the plants
One plant has evolved to be taller in the brighter light
mcqs.explain: The genome and its interaction with the environment influence the development of the phenotype, so the different light conditions have produced different heights.

mcqs.q: Which of these describes the causes of variation between individuals in a population?
options: Inherited genes, the conditions of development, or both
Inherited genes alone, which are passed on by the parents
Mutations that are produced by a change in the environment
Mutations alone, because every one changes the phenotype
mcqs.explain: Variation may be due to the genes they have inherited, the conditions in which they have developed, or a combination of genes and the environment.

mcqs.q: All variants arise from mutations. Which statement about mutations and phenotype is correct?
options: Most mutations lead to a change in the phenotype
Most mutations have no effect on the phenotype
Mutations happen only when the environment changes
Mutations build up in an organism during its life
mcqs.explain: Most variants have no effect on the phenotype, some influence phenotype and very few determine phenotype.

mcqs.q: A mutation produces a new phenotype in a population. The environment then changes, and the new phenotype is suited to the new conditions. What is the likely result?
options: More mutations of this type occur in the population
A relatively rapid change in the species can take place
Each organism changes to the new phenotype in its lifetime
The organisms develop the new phenotype that they need
mcqs.explain: If the new phenotype is suited to an environmental change it can lead to a relatively rapid change in the species.

options: A change in the characteristics of an animal during its lifetime
A change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time
A change in appearance that makes a population a new species
The growth of the characteristics that organisms need most
mcqs.explain: Evolution is a change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time through a process of natural selection.

mcqs.q: In a beetle population most beetles are pale and a few are dark. The tree bark the beetles live on becomes darker, so birds find the pale beetles more easily. After many generations most of the beetles are dark. Which statement explains this?
options: The beetles developed a darker colour because they needed it
Each pale beetle became darker as the tree bark grew darker
The darker bark caused the mutations that made beetles darker
Dark beetles survived to breed and passed on their variant
mcqs.explain: Natural selection acts on variants that give rise to phenotypes best suited to their environment, and those beetles pass the genes on to the next generation.

mcqs.q: Two populations of one species have been separated for a very long time and now look very different. What must be shown before they are classed as two new species?
options: That their phenotypes are different enough to tell apart
That each population has developed the features that it needs
That the individuals have changed during their own lifetimes
That they can no longer produce fertile offspring together
mcqs.explain: Two new species have formed when the populations are so different in phenotype that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

mcqs.q: A farmer chooses the cows that produce the most milk and breeds them together. From their offspring he again breeds those that produce the most milk, and he repeats this for many generations. Which statement about this process is correct?
options: It is natural selection, as the best cows survive and breed
It is genetic engineering, as the genome is being modified
It is selective breeding, as the farmer chose the parents
It was complete once the first chosen cows had been bred
mcqs.explain: Selective breeding is the process by which humans breed animals for particular genetic characteristics, here the useful characteristic of producing more milk.

mcqs.q: Which statement about selective breeding is correct?
options: It removes inherited defects from the breeds produced
It happens in the wild without human choice
It can lead to inbreeding in the breeds it produces
It adds a new gene from another organism to the offspring
mcqs.explain: Selective breeding can lead to 'inbreeding' where some breeds are particularly prone to disease or inherited defects.

options: A gene is transferred into the cells of another organism
Parents with the desired characteristic are bred together
Cells from one organism are grown into identical copies
A faulty gene in a patient is fixed to cure a disorder
mcqs.explain: Genes from the chromosomes of humans and other organisms can be 'cut out' and transferred to cells of other organisms, modifying the genome.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the uses of genetic engineering is correct?
options: Bacterial cells have been genetically engineered to make human insulin
Tissue culture is used to add genes to bacterial cells
Inherited disorders are now cured using genetic modification
Crops are engineered by breeding the best plants together
mcqs.explain: Bacterial cells have been genetically engineered to produce useful substances such as human insulin to treat diabetes.

mcqs.q: Which statement about genetically modified (GM) crops is correct?
options: GM crops generally produce lower yields than other food crops
GM crops are grown from cells taken from one parent plant
GM crops may affect wild flower and insect populations
GM crops are used to treat inherited disorders in patients
mcqs.explain: Concerns about GM crops include the effect on populations of wild flowers and insects, and some people feel the effects on human health have not been fully explored.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes the main steps in the process of genetic engineering?
options: Enzymes isolate the gene, which a vector puts into cells
Enzymes cut out the gene and carry it into the cells
Cells are taken from an organism and grown into copies
The best parent organisms are bred to combine genes
mcqs.explain: Enzymes are used to isolate the required gene, this gene is inserted into a vector, usually a bacterial plasmid or a virus, and the vector is used to insert the gene into the required cells at an early stage of their development.
